design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (real_estate_closing_plans, category realty), round 2. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[4, 5]; the failed-sale charge takes 5 factors, the first settlement payment takes 4.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. A seller who withdrew her listing a week ago wants to settle what she owes for listing-period repairs, spread over a few months, paying the first part by card. The settlement rule says the payment 'is not taken until the order's billing history carries the failed-sale charge invoice billed for that service'; the ledger has none, so the agent must find the one write that books it (the failed-sale charge), price it from the order's ledgers and two other products, and only then work out the settlement plan's first payment from the seller's payment history, tenure and billing channel on other Bridgewell products. Difficulty comes from reading rules, reconciling ledgers and calculating; the tools are two atomic writes.

2. SCOPE. Task 0 claims the seller side: realty_ext_failed_sale_charge (target bill_failed_sale_charge_3e9b31c4, event realty_seller_service_charge) and realty_ext_seller_settlement_payment (target pay_failed_sale_charge_by_card_a1a6aa51, event realty_payment, seller). Task 1 claims the buyer side before closing (reissued plan invoice and buyer direct card payment) with its own tools; no asset overlaps.

3. POLICIES AND FACTOR CARD.
realty_ext_failed_sale_charge: base_policy_refs [realty_failed_sale_charges]; trigger state_due (a cancelled, never-closed listing order with seller-phase benefit owes the charge; this order was cancelled on 2026-09-08 and the first month end after it has not passed at frozen_time). Overwrite: the base lesser-of sentence is replaced by 'The failed-sale charge billed on an order is the amount this paragraph works out in place of the plain lesser-of amount, no failed-sale charge is billed when the seller-phase benefit paid is zero, and seller service call fees already collected never reduce it.' (whole scope of the base policy). Every other base clause (status listing_expired/cancelled and never closed, one per order, never on buyer-only orders, due failed_sale_bill_due_days after billing) is restated. Baseline: lesser of plan premium invoiced and seller-phase benefit paid -> 1495.0. All five adjustments are part of the billed charge itself, so nothing is left unbooked.
 - listing_cap_proration (method; date): 127 days in force -> months-begun proration, cap 1245.83; daily proration under 60 days, full premium at 180+. Baseline -> 1056.75.
 - after_hours_dispatch_recovery (parameter; history): the after-hours rate is set by the costliest trade dispatched after hours: one of the two emergency requests was hvac -> 95.00 each = 190.0 (only non-hvac emergencies -> 70.00 each). Near-miss: the routine water heater, dishwasher and garage door requests do not count. Baseline -> 727.37.
 - maintained_hvac_credit (parameter; reads the seller's hvaccare agreement and visits; hvaccare is not a category any difficulty claims, so this factor is not counted as cross-difficulty, cross_difficulty null; multi-source address AND visit count): 2 tune-ups in twelve months -> share 0.2 of net HVAC benefit = 236.0; more tune-ups give the larger share. Near-miss: tune-up 2025-09-10 is twelve months and five days before the billing date and is excluded. Baseline -> 1046.87.
 - missed_contact_service_credit (parameter; history): one re-dispatch after a missed contact window -> 40.00 (two or more -> 75.00). Baseline -> 899.87.
 - keep_home_waiver (parameter; cross-difficulty homeplan, a category the homeowner difficulty claims; multi-source start-date window AND tier monthly premium): HomeCare Silver started 3 days after end_date, monthly premium 62.99 < 70.00 -> 0.25. Baseline -> 1159.83.
 Result 869.87.
realty_ext_seller_settlement_payment: base_policy_refs [realty_closing_and_escrow (governs realty_payment), realty_failed_sale_charges]; trigger on_request (the seller asks to spread the charge). Overwrite, scoped: the base sentence 'The charge is billed to the seller and due failed_sale_bill_due_days calendar days after billing.' is replaced, only for a charge the seller asks to spread, by the settlement plan (first payment now, the rest in equal monthly installments, the first on the charge's due date); every other failed-sale charge stays due as base says. Baseline: pay the open failed-sale balance in full as the first payment -> 869.87. No allowance or credit is taken at payment; the part not paid now stays open on the failed-sale invoice as the scheduled installment, so the ledger after the call agrees with the plan.
 - settlement_installments (method; history; balance band, applied when the plan is set up, before any seller payment on the order): balance 869.87 in (400, 900] -> two installments, first = half the amount after the down payment rounded up; above 900 -> three, first = amount less two thirds rounded down; otherwise unsplit. Baseline -> 869.87.
 - payment_history_down_payment (parameter; cross-difficulty lineplan + homeplan returned payments): one returned payment (line plan, billed back 2026-03-04) -> 0.15; two or more -> 0.30. Baseline -> 456.68.
 - coverage_tenure_down_payment (parameter; cross-difficulty lineplan; date): earliest active plan is the line plan from 2025-12-01, 9 whole months -> 0.10 (under 6 months or none -> 0.25; 24+ -> none). The homeowner contract is in waiting_period, not active, and does not count. Baseline -> 478.43.
 - autopay_down_payment_relief (parameter; cross-difficulty lineplan billing channel): billed automatically to a card -> 0.05 (bank draft -> 0.10; utility bill or none -> 0). Baseline -> 543.67.
 Result 521.92. Every tier rests on seeded records (the charge amount, the seller's payment rows, the line plan and homeowner rows); none is fixed by the billing write's own date.

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Charge write: realty_failed_sale_charges.failed_sale_only_on_unclosed_order — status cancelled, closing_date empty on 58622c13-f20c-4edc-8009-e5dfc1fd788b; one_failed_sale_charge_per_order — no realty_seller_service_charge row on 58622c13-f20c-4edc-8009-e5dfc1fd788b. No time gate. Payment write: realty_closing_and_escrow has no gate applying to realty_payment -> policy_scope; the only open invoice after the billing write is the failed-sale invoice, so 'Payments are applied to the oldest open invoice first' lands it there.

5. WORLD ROWS. customers: the seller. realty_contracts: the cancelled listing order (order 2026-05-04, cancelled 2026-09-08; listing agent license 2017003318 on the order). billing: plan invoice 1,495.00, order_cancelled credit 1,495.00 (nothing paid, so no credit balance or refund), five seller fees of 75.00. requests and 15 claim events: 2,030.00 authorized, 240.00 reversed (garage door repair declined), two emergencies (one hvac), one re-dispatch, two not-covered determinations. service_contractors: the six contractors on the dispatches and tune-ups. homeplan contract (Silver, waiting_period, started 2026-09-11) + first installment and its payment: keep-home waiver tier and tenure exclusion. hvaccare agreement + 3 tune-ups: maintained-system tier and near-miss. lineplan (card-billed, from 2025-12-01) + 23 billing rows including one returned payment, its fee and the repayment: payment-history, tenure and autopay tiers. Automatic clauses checked: the cancellation credit memo is present (order_cancelled trigger); no rider exists for the addon trigger; no fee refund is owed (every request was dispatched); the homeowner first installment is paid; the line plan and maintenance agreement are current; the failed-sale charge is not yet owed past a month end.

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target: the failed-sale charge on order 58622c13-f20c-4edc-8009-e5dfc1fd788b and the seller's first settlement payment against the invoice it creates (FS-C8A1BAB2B7). Included: every billing/claim/request row with realty_contract_id 58622c13-f20c-4edc-8009-e5dfc1fd788b. Excluded: the credited plan invoice 2605044417 as an object of payment. The reversal 2605221190 settles only authorization 2605221190. The payment carries invoice_number FS-C8A1BAB2B7.

7. PERSONA. Odalys, a pharmacist on a break: volunteers the goal (settle the listing-period repairs, spread if allowed, first part by card), the property and that she withdrew the listing on September 8. Gives phone/ZIP/email when asked; other coverage, the March bounced line plan payment and its repayment when asked; says she has paid nothing earlier when asked. Passive reactions: agrees if told something must be put on her account first; accepts the figure the agent says is due today; runs the handed-over payment exactly; closes. She names no figure, no invoice and no mechanism.

8. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root realty_ext_seller_settlement_payment (owner=user tool pay_failed_sale_charge_by_card_a1a6aa51); prerequisite realty_ext_failed_sale_charge (owner=agent tool bill_failed_sale_charge_3e9b31c4). Edge kind value_input, gate failed_sale_billed, form state, sentence (negated direction): "A seller's settlement payment toward listing-period service is not taken until the order's billing history carries the failed-sale charge invoice billed for that service.". Four-point test: connective 'not ... until'; record-visible state (a failed-sale charge invoice on the order's billing history); no tool, id or code token; scope exactly one failed-sale invoice per order. Exactly one write in this difficulty books a failed-sale charge invoice (bill_failed_sale_charge_3e9b31c4 under realty_ext_failed_sale_charge). False at opening (ledger rows 563baf7a-cd7d-4845-a221-06e8b47cfc2c, 0e9a28e5-390f-4c46-b918-8c40004f0f60, fee rows only); flips at step 14. Order [realty_ext_failed_sale_charge, realty_ext_seller_settlement_payment]. Deletion sensitivity: payment 0.0 instead of 521.92.

9. LONG AND BROAD; EASY MISTAKES. Depth: payment -> waits on charge invoice -> charge. Breadth: order dates, three order ledgers, hvaccare visits, homeplan start and tier, line plan returned payments, start date and billing channel. Mistakes: billing the plain lesser-of 1495.0; counting the 2025-09-10 tune-up; counting the reversed garage-door repair; applying the general after-hours rate; treating the waiting-period homeowner contract as active tenure; skipping the down payment; paying the whole balance; paying before billing.

10. STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION. Reads: customer, verify (phone + ZIP), realty contract, billing, requests, claim events, contractors, homeplan contract and billing, hvaccare agreement and visits, line plan and billing. Write 1 (step 14): bill_failed_sale_charge_3e9b31c4(realty_contract_id=58622c13-f20c-4edc-8009-e5dfc1fd788b, amount=869.87, due_date=2026-10-15) -> invoice FS-C8A1BAB2B7. Write 2 (step 16): unlock and hand over pay_failed_sale_charge_by_card_a1a6aa51(realty_contract_id=58622c13-f20c-4edc-8009-e5dfc1fd788b, invoice_number=FS-C8A1BAB2B7, amount=521.92). Scratch verifier replays gold with the real tools and evaluates both computes with check_compute's sandbox: charge 869.87; payment 521.92; per-factor baselines charge [('listing_cap_proration', 1056.75), ('after_hours_dispatch_recovery', 727.37), ('maintained_hvac_credit', 1046.87), ('missed_contact_service_credit', 899.87), ('keep_home_waiver', 1159.83)]; payment [('settlement_installments', 869.87), ('payment_history_down_payment', 456.68), ('coverage_tenure_down_payment', 478.43), ('autopay_down_payment_relief', 543.67)]; all-baseline charge 1495.0, payment 869.87; skip-billing payment 0.0.

11. SOLVABILITY AND DRAFT RECOMPUTE. Step 14 cites cancelled status, empty closing date and the ledger without a failed-sale row; step 16 rests on prior_step 14. Draft from visible text only: payment rule -> needs a failed-sale invoice -> charge 1245.83 + 190 - 236 - 40 = 1159.83 x 0.75 = 869.87 -> settlement: down share 0.15 + 0.10 - 0.05 = 0.20 -> 173.97; two installments of the rest, first 347.95 -> 521.92. Agrees with gold.

12. REVISION LOG (round 2, from the policy-task audit). F1: the settlement allowances and credit left part of the charge unbooked -> removed from the payment; the missed-contact credit moved into the billed charge; the payment is now a scheduled first payment with the rest open as installments, under a scoped overwrite of the base due-date sentence. F3: the prompt settlement allowance rested on the billing write's own date -> removed; the payment's factors now rest on seeded records. O9: the falling per-emergency rate and the uncovered-fee credit share rising with denials were replaced (after-hours rate by costliest trade; uncovered-fee credit dropped). O8: hvaccare is no longer labelled cross-difficulty. O3: the tool docstrings no longer mention when the invoice number is used. O5: compute_basis.result now quotes the sentence that combines the down payment and first installment. O6: the unstated '> 0' test is gone. O10: the order was cancelled one week before the call, before the first month end. Persona no longer scripts an installment outcome. The 'exactly twelve months' wording is gone. Gate log after the rebuild is in the final difficulty run (all gates OK; traceability lists only the unlock tool names, which have no source before the KB exists).
 ROUND 3 (render notes and re-audit observations): R2-O1 — the 'no earlier seller payment' conjunct is moved out of the installment ladder into the plan's scope ('The settlement plan is set up once, before the seller has made any payment on the order'); the ladder now selects by the balance band alone, so settlement_installments is no longer counted as multi-source (the task keeps the keep-home, maintained-system and after-hours factors as multi-source). Item 6 — the card payment tool docstring now says it records a payment with method card and no longer claims to charge a card on the profile. No scored value moved; gates re-run on the final form.
user_scenario: You are Odalys Pemberton-Quayle, a soft-spoken hospital pharmacist in Dublin, Ohio, calling Bridgewell on a short break between shifts, so you are polite but keep things moving. In May your listing agent ordered a Bridgewell real estate plan with seller coverage when you put your house at 4471 Larkspur Bend Drive, Dublin, OH 43017 on the market. Last week, on September 8, you took the house off the market because you decided to stay. While it was listed Bridgewell sent people out for a few problems, the upstairs air conditioning among them. You open by saying you understand that because the house never sold you owe Bridgewell for the repairs it handled while the house was listed, and that you would like to spread what you owe over a few months if Bridgewell allows that, and pay the first part today on the card you have on file with Bridgewell. You do not know any amount, any invoice number or how the figure is worked out, and you never guess one. When the agent asks who you are, you give your full name and your phone number, 6145550127; if the agent wants a second detail you give your mailing ZIP code, 43017, and if asked for your email you spell it out as odalys.pembertonquayle@larkspurmail.com. If the agent asks which property or which plan, you describe the Larkspur Bend Drive listing you took off the market on September 8. Only if the agent asks about your other Bridgewell coverage do you say that you signed up for a homeowner plan on the same house a few days after taking it off the market, that you have had a Comfort Care heating and cooling maintenance membership on the house for a couple of years with tune-ups last fall and this spring, and that you have carried the water service line plan since last December, billed automatically to your card; if asked about missed payments you say one line plan payment bounced back in March and you paid it again a few days later. You do not remember prices or other dates. If the agent asks whether you have paid anything toward the listing-period repairs before, you say no, nothing yet. If the agent explains that something has to be put on your account before you can pay, you say that is fine and ask them to go ahead. When the agent tells you how much is due from you today, you accept that figure. Payment is something you do yourself: when the agent hands the card payment over to you with the plan number, invoice number and amount, you make that payment exactly as given, then read back the confirmation number it gives you if asked. Once the payment has gone through, you thank the agent and say goodbye.
